title: Interrupted suturing and wound closure on a skin pad

guidelineVersions: Northern Care Alliance suture care leaflet (Jan 2026)

related.id: MB-143 Excision of a skin lesion
related.why: The same local anaesthetic and closure

brief.setting: Emergency department, minor injuries; on a skin pad
brief.scenario: Mr Tom Reilly, 34, cut the back of his left forearm on a kitchen knife 2 hours ago. The bleeding has stopped with pressure. He is fit and right-handed. A skin pad, a suture pack, lidocaine 1% with adrenaline, saline and a choice of sutures are provided.
brief.task: Assess the wound, then close the laceration on the skin pad with interrupted sutures, talking the examiner through each step. Answer the examiner's questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Safe to close here? Then anaesthetise, handle skin gently, evert, square knots, sharps away, removal date.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Crushing the skin edges with forceps, or tying tight knots that invert the edges.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll confirm who he is, how and when it happened, and check his hand before any anaesthetic."

grid.label: Checks, consent and tetanus
grid.fail: Starts without confirming identity, mechanism, allergies or tetanus status.
grid.pass: Confirms identity, mechanism, allergies and anticoagulants; verbal consent. Clean wound under 6 hours after a primary course: no vaccine needed.
grid.high: States that uncertain immunisation needs an immediate reinforcing dose, and a high-risk wound may also need immunoglobulin.

grid.label: Wound assessment and cleaning
grid.fail: Closes without examining the wound or checking hand function.
grid.pass: Checks sensation, movement and circulation before anaesthetic; explores for foreign body and tendon injury; irrigates with saline.
grid.high: Would X-ray for glass or metal, and refer tendon, nerve or vessel injury rather than close it here.

grid.label: Local anaesthetic
grid.fail: Injects without checking allergy or the maximum dose.
grid.pass: Checks allergy and maximum dose; aspirates; infiltrates through the wound edges; tests before starting.
grid.high: States the 500 mg maximum with adrenaline, and that adrenaline is contraindicated in fingers, toes, nose tip, ears and penis.

grid.label: Asepsis and set-up
grid.fail: Contaminates the field or works without sterile gloves.
grid.pass: Hand hygiene, sterile gloves, cleans and drapes; instruments and sharps bin within reach.
grid.high: Positions the arm and light first, and arranges the tray so the needle is always on the holder or in a safe zone.

grid.label: Instrument handling
grid.fail: Grips the needle at the swage or tip; crushes the skin edge with forceps.
grid.pass: Thumb and ring finger in the needle holder; needle held one-third to one-half from the swage; toothed forceps lift the dermis gently.
grid.high: Enters the skin perpendicular and follows the curve of the needle by rotating the wrist.

grid.label: Suture choice, eversion and knots
grid.fail: Chooses silk or a braided absorbable; inverts the edges; ties granny knots over the wound.
grid.borderline: The edges meet but are flat or inverted, and the knots sit on the wound line.
grid.pass: 4-0 non-absorbable monofilament (e.g. nylon); everted edges; equal bites and spacing; square instrument-tied knots laid to one side.
grid.high: Approximates without strangling the edges, allowing for swelling; knows a granny knot slips and extra throws add bulk, not strength.

grid.label: Sharps (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Leaves the needle loose on the field, or recaps a needle.
grid.pass: Keeps the needle on the holder, handles it with instruments, and disposes of sharps at the point of use.
grid.high: Never recaps; after a needlestick: first aid, report it, and urgent occupational health advice about prophylaxis.

grid.label: Aftercare and safety-netting
grid.fail: Gives no wound care, removal date or warning signs.
grid.pass: Dressing; keep clean and dry; sutures out at 7–10 days on the forearm; return for redness, discharge, pain or temperature above 38°C.
grid.high: Knows other sites (face 5 days; back and over joints 10–14 days); no swimming until healed; sun protection for the scar.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Can I confirm your name and date of birth? Kitchen knife, 2 hours ago? Allergies or blood thinners? [No.] Tetanus: all childhood vaccines, last at school. It's a clean wound under 6 hours, so no vaccine. If he didn't know his status, he'd need a reinforcing dose now; a dirty wound might also need immunoglobulin. Happy for me to stitch it?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Tests sensation, each finger extensor, capillary refill.] Normal. [Explores under a good light.] No tendon or foreign body. With glass I'd X-ray it, and a tendon or nerve injury would go to the hand team. [Irrigates with saline.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Lidocaine with adrenaline: the maximum is 500 mg, and he needs a few millilitres. On a finger I'd use plain lidocaine; adrenaline is contraindicated there. [Aspirates, infiltrates through the edges, waits, tests.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Positions the arm and light, hand hygiene, sterile gloves, cleans, drapes; sets a safe zone for the needle.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Needle held a third of the way from the swage.] I enter perpendicular and follow the curve by rotating my wrist, lifting the dermis, not crushing the epidermis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: 4-0 nylon. [Everted edges, equal bites, square knots laid to one side.] Just apposed, not strangled, because it will swell. A granny knot slips, and extra throws only add bulk.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Needle stays on the holder; into the sharps bin at the point of use; no recapping.] If I had a needlestick: first aid, report it, and occupational health straight away.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Out in 7 to 10 days on the forearm; a face would be 5, a back 10 to 14. Keep it dry, no swimming until healed, and protect the scar from the sun. Come back with spreading redness, discharge or a temperature over 38.

failures.move: Closing without checking hand function or exploring the wound.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: a tendon or nerve injury, or a foreign body, is sealed in.

failures.move: Leaving the needle on the drape or recapping it.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: needlestick risk to the operator and the team.

failures.move: Crushing the skin edge with toothed forceps.
failures.consequence: Tissue damage, poor healing and a worse scar.

failures.move: Tight knots that invert the edges.
failures.consequence: Inverted edges heal into a depressed, wider scar.

recovery.when: You're asked the dose and aren't sure
recovery.line: I'd check the product information before injecting: with adrenaline, the maximum single dose of lidocaine is 500 mg.
That's a granny knot. I'll replace the suture and square the throws.

knowledge.fact: Clean wound: under 6 hours, non-penetrating, negligible tissue damage. Primed, last dose over 10 years ago: clean wound none; tetanus-prone, reinforcing dose. Uncertain status: reinforcing dose.
Lidocaine with adrenaline: maximum single dose 500 mg; vasoconstrictor contraindicated in fingers, toes, nose tip, ears and penis.
Suture size: 4-0 or 5-0 on limbs, 5-0 or 6-0 on the face; enter at 90 degrees to evert.
Grasp the needle one-third to one-half from the swage; square knots, not granny knots.
Removal: face 5 days; scalp 7; arms, legs, hands 7–10; back and over joints 10–14.
Needles are not recapped; secure sharps containers close to where sharps are used (reg 5).

recall.think: Is this wound safe to close here?
recall.say: "Clean, under 6 hours, hand intact: I'll close it."
recall.trap: Crushing the skin edge with forceps.

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading; introduce yourself, explain the task, confirm identity and obtain consent at every station

sources.name: UKHSA: Guidance on the management of suspected tetanus cases and the assessment and management of tetanus-prone wounds
sources.supports: A clean wound is less than 6 hours old, non-penetrating, with negligible tissue damage (Table 4, note 1); adequate priming course but last dose more than 10 years ago: clean wound none required, tetanus-prone wound an immediate reinforcing dose, high-risk tetanus-prone wound a reinforcing dose plus human tetanus immunoglobulin; uncertain immunisation status: immediate reinforcing dose even for a clean wound, plus human tetanus immunoglobulin for a tetanus-prone or high-risk tetanus-prone wound (Table 4); 5 doses at appropriate intervals give lifelong immunity (7.1); high-risk features include heavy contamination (e.g. soil or manure), surgery delayed more than 6 hours, extensive devitalised tissue (7.2)

sources.name: Lidocaine 1% with adrenaline 1:200,000 solution for injection: Summary of Product Characteristics (emc 2397)
sources.supports: Maximum single dose of lidocaine given with adrenaline: 500 mg (4.2); vasoconstrictor contraindicated for anaesthesia of fingers, toes, tip of nose, ears and penis (4.3); aspirate before and during injection (4.2)

sources.name: Forsch RT. Essentials of skin laceration repair. Am Fam Physician 2008;78(8):945–951
sources.supports: Suture size: 3-0 or 4-0 on the trunk, 4-0 or 5-0 on the extremities and scalp, 5-0 or 6-0 on the face; the needle pierces the skin at 90 degrees, with the suture following the curve of the needle, to evert the edges; copious irrigation with normal saline or tap water

sources.name: Ethicon: Wound Closure Manual
sources.supports: Grasp the needle one-third to one-half of the distance from the swaged end to the point, avoiding the swage; the two-hand square knot is the most reliable; incorrectly crossed strands make a granny knot, which tends to slip; extra throws add bulk, not strength, to a properly squared knot; skin edges should be everted; interrupted technique usually preferred

sources.name: Health and Safety (Sharp Instruments in Healthcare) Regulations 2013 (SI 2013/645)
sources.supports: Employers must ensure needles are not capped after use unless a risk assessment requires it and a suitable device controls the risk, and that secure sharps containers are close to where sharps are used (reg 5(1)); after a sharps injury with possible exposure, the employer must ensure immediate medical advice and any post-exposure prophylaxis (reg 7(2))

sources.name: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust: Emergency and Urgent Care – Care of Sutures/Stitches (patient information PI_M_738)
sources.version: Leaflet dated January 2026; page updated 8 January 2026
sources.supports: Time guide for suture removal: head and scalp 7 days; face 5 days; arms, legs, hands and fingers 7 to 10 days; over joints 10 to 14 days; back 10 to 14 days; keep stitches dry; no swimming or sport until healed; return for worsening or foul-smelling discharge, heat, redness, swelling or pain, feeling unwell or shivery, or a temperature above 38.0°C; protect the healed wound from sun for 6 to 12 months

partner.opening: Please assess this wound and close it on the skin pad, talking me through what you are doing.

reveals.finding: Identity confirmed. Kitchen knife 2 hours ago. No allergies, no anticoagulants, 78 kg. He agrees to stitches.
"I had all my childhood jabs. The last one was at school, when I was about 14."
4 cm linear cut into fat, clean edges, no debris, no tendon visible. Sensation, finger extension and capillary refill normal.
Watch the needle grip, the forceps on the dermis, and whether the edges evert.

push.question: Why a non-absorbable monofilament here?
push.expect: Low tissue reaction and infection risk on the skin; comes out cleanly at removal.

push.question: What is the maximum dose of your local anaesthetic?
push.expect: Lidocaine with adrenaline: 500 mg maximum single dose.

push.question: When do these come out, and where?
push.expect: 7–10 days for the forearm, by the practice nurse.

curveballs.prompt: The cut is on his finger instead.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Plain lidocaine without adrenaline: a vasoconstrictor is contraindicated in fingers.

curveballs.prompt: He can't remember ever having a tetanus vaccine.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Uncertain status: an immediate reinforcing dose, even for a clean wound; a tetanus-prone wound also needs tetanus immunoglobulin.

curveballs.prompt: It happened on a farm 12 hours ago and there's soil in it.
curveballs.safeAnswer: High-risk tetanus-prone: thorough cleaning and debridement, reinforcing dose plus tetanus immunoglobulin; discuss with a senior whether to close.

curveballs.prompt: You get a needlestick while tying.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop; first aid; replace gloves; report it and get urgent occupational health advice about prophylaxis.
